## Code Review

This pull request introduces an optimization for MoE models using tensor and sequence parallelism by replacing an `all_reduce` operation with a more efficient `reduce_scatter`. This is implemented as a `torch.compile` pass that pattern-matches the common sequence of `all_reduce` -> `rmsnorm` -> `sequence_parallel_chunk`. A new `reduce_scatter_with_padding` collective is added to handle sequence lengths not divisible by the tensor-parallel world size. The changes are well-structured, include robust configuration checks to enable the pass only when appropriate, and are accompanied by thorough tests that validate correctness across different scenarios. I have reviewed the changes and found no high or critical issues.

This applicability check still disables the pass whenever `compile_range.end` is not divisible by TP under piecewise compilation, even though this commit introduces `reduce_scatter_with_padding` specifically to handle non-divisible sequence lengths. As written, odd-size compile ranges in the default piecewise path skip the optimization entirely, negating the intended improvement for those batches.

My understanding is that `SP` here is only applied to the MoE `hidden_states` path.
The decoder residual sits at the layer boundary, and it’s expected to stay **full-sized** across layers, since it’s passed into the next layer’s `fused add + RMSNorm`. 
In the replacement, I chunk the residual to match the local `reduce_scatter` computation. 
After that, I all-gather it back so the layer interface remains unchanged.
The final trim just removes the tail padding rows that were introduced during chunking when the sequence length isn’t divisible by the parallel size. It doesn’t drop any real tokens.
But this does introduce extra communication, which is not aligned with our original goal of minimizing communication overhead. So I’m quite confused about this.
